1.modern-en: Caius Martius confronts the rioting plebeians in the Roman street and insults them at length before being called away to the Volscian war.

4.modern-en: Caius Martius leads the assault on Corioles, is driven back, and rallies the army with the most furious speech of his career.

5.modern-en: Caius Martius enters the gates of Corioles almost alone and is trapped inside while his men hold back.

6.modern-en: Caius Martius emerges from Corioles, bloodied, and rejoins the Roman line.

7.modern-en: Caius Martius fights Aufidius in single combat outside Corioles and is dragged off the field by his men.

8.modern-en: Caius Martius is honoured by Cominius after the battle, refuses the title of plunder, and is given the surname Coriolanus.

9.modern-en: Coriolanus, now home, is greeted by his mother and wife and then proposed for consul.

11.modern-en: Coriolanus stands in the Capitol while Cominius recites his deeds and is unanimously chosen consul, on condition he stand in the marketplace in the gown of humility.

13.modern-en: Coriolanus, in the gown of humility, asks the citizens for their voices with poorly concealed contempt and is given them anyway.

14.modern-en: Coriolanus learns that the tribunes have stirred the citizens to withdraw their voices and explodes at the news.

15.modern-en: Coriolanus returns to the marketplace and is provoked by Sicinius into calling the people 'curs,' which is taken as treason.

17.modern-en: Coriolanus is recalled to the marketplace by his mother and Menenius to apologise, but lets Sicinius bait him into refusing.

18.modern-en: Coriolanus is banished from Rome; his last lines to the city are 'I banish you.'

19.modern-en: Coriolanus takes leave of his mother, wife, son, and friends at the city gate and walks out alone.

22.modern-en: Coriolanus, disguised in mean clothes, arrives at Aufidius's house in Antium and offers his throat or his service.

23.modern-en: Coriolanus and Aufidius dine together and embrace; the Volscian servants admire the new alliance.

25.modern-en: Coriolanus, encamped outside Rome, refuses Cominius's embassy of peace.

26.modern-en: Coriolanus refuses Menenius's later embassy with even greater coldness.

28.modern-en: Coriolanus is broken by his mother's appeal in front of the Volscian army, calls off the assault, and embraces her.

29.modern-en: Coriolanus is met in the Volscian city by Aufidius's accusations of treachery and is killed on the spot by Aufidius's conspirators.

epithet.en: Coriolanus's mother, the play's iron Roman matron

3.modern-en: Volumnia tells Virgilia she would rather have eleven sons die nobly in war than one live in idle pleasure.

9.modern-en: Volumnia greets her son on his return from Corioles, counts his new wounds, and tells him he must be consul next.

11.modern-en: Volumnia is in the Capitol pressing the consulship on Coriolanus.

14.modern-en: Volumnia urges her son to take the gown of humility and dissemble for the people, against his nature.

16.modern-en: Volumnia briefly storms at the tribunes for ruining her son.

18.modern-en: Volumnia delivers a long curse at Sicinius in the street after the banishment is announced.

19.modern-en: Volumnia takes leave of Coriolanus at the city gate.

25.modern-en: Volumnia gathers herself, Virgilia, and the small boy and walks out of Rome to meet her son at the Volscian camp.

28.modern-en: Volumnia kneels in front of Coriolanus, leads Virgilia and the boy to kneel beside her, and breaks her son's resolution with a long speech and a long silence.

epithet.en: Patrician senator and Coriolanus's surrogate father

1.modern-en: Menenius tells the rioting citizens the fable of the belly to talk them down before Caius Martius arrives.

7.modern-en: Menenius is at the Roman senate during the rejoicing for the Corioles victory.

10.modern-en: Menenius greets Coriolanus on his triumphal return with affectionate banter.

11.modern-en: Menenius shepherds Coriolanus through the consulship vote in the Capitol.

14.modern-en: Menenius urges Coriolanus to bend a little to the people.

18.modern-en: Menenius watches the banishment helplessly and has to send Coriolanus off.

19.modern-en: Menenius is at the gate with the family to take leave of Coriolanus.

25.modern-en: Menenius volunteers to go alone to the Volscian camp to plead with Coriolanus and is humiliated when he is dismissed.

epithet.en: The Volscian general, Coriolanus's lifelong enemy

2.modern-en: Aufidius is shown in the Volscian Senate at Corioles preparing for war with Rome.

9.modern-en: Aufidius is reported as having retreated after the loss of Corioles and the duel with Caius Martius.

10.modern-en: Aufidius vows in a private scene at Antium that he will have Coriolanus by any means — fair or foul.

22.modern-en: Aufidius receives the disguised Coriolanus in his house, embraces him as a brother, and offers him joint command of the Volscian army.

23.modern-en: Aufidius shares his command with Coriolanus and watches his servants and lieutenants begin to prefer the newcomer.

25.modern-en: Aufidius is at Coriolanus's side as he refuses the Roman embassies and grows quietly jealous of his ascendancy.

26.modern-en: Aufidius watches Coriolanus humiliate Menenius and stores up the moment.

28.modern-en: Aufidius witnesses Volumnia break Coriolanus's resolution and realises he can now destroy his rival politically.

29.modern-en: Aufidius accuses Coriolanus of treachery before the Volscian council and orders the conspirators to cut him down.

1.modern-en: Sicinius is appointed tribune at the end of the opening riot, with Brutus, as a concession to the plebeians.

11.modern-en: Sicinius watches the consulship vote in the Capitol with thinly veiled hostility.

12.modern-en: Sicinius confers with Brutus on how to use the marketplace ritual against Coriolanus.

14.modern-en: Sicinius engineers the recall of the citizens' voices and lectures the patricians on the people's will.

15.modern-en: Sicinius provokes Coriolanus into his outburst on 'the common cry of curs.'

17.modern-en: Sicinius drags Coriolanus back into the marketplace and presses the charge of treason.

18.modern-en: Sicinius pronounces sentence: banishment for life on pain of death.

24.modern-en: Sicinius is in Rome during the early reports of Coriolanus's revenge.

25.modern-en: Sicinius is at the senate when the news arrives that the Volscian army stands at the gates.

1.modern-en: Brutus is named tribune at the end of the opening riot.

11.modern-en: Brutus watches the consulship vote and signals to the citizens what they should think later.

12.modern-en: Brutus plans with Sicinius the ambush in the marketplace.

14.modern-en: Brutus presses the case against Coriolanus among the tribunes and the people.

15.modern-en: Brutus eggs Sicinius on as Coriolanus is brought to fury in the marketplace.

17.modern-en: Brutus seconds the charge of treason and helps drive Coriolanus into his fatal outburst.

18.modern-en: Brutus voices the formal banishment with Sicinius.

24.modern-en: Brutus is in Rome as the early reports of the Volscian march come in, brushing them aside as scaremongering.

3.modern-en: Virgilia is at home with Volumnia, refusing to play visitors while her husband is at the wars.

11.modern-en: Virgilia stands silently with Volumnia at the Capitol vote.

14.modern-en: Virgilia listens to her mother-in-law and son talk over Coriolanus's political crisis without saying much.

19.modern-en: Virgilia stands with her son and her mother-in-law at the city gate to take leave of Coriolanus.

25.modern-en: Virgilia kneels with Volumnia in front of Coriolanus at the Volscian camp, and Coriolanus's silence over her is part of what breaks him.

16.modern-en: Young Martius is described to his grandmother as having torn apart a butterfly in his nursery, a comic-grim foreshadowing of his father.

25.modern-en: Young Martius is brought with Volumnia and Virgilia to plead with Coriolanus at the Volscian camp.

28.modern-en: Young Martius stands silently between his mother and grandmother as Coriolanus is finally broken.
